annotations.text:
Where this stands

The robot direction replaces everything to the right of this note — those artboards are the previous identity, kept only until the new one is drawn.

The tray styles above are redrawn from your reference on the pixel grid. The logo is not drawn yet: the file you sent is 310×237 with the navy background baked in and no alpha, which is well below what an app icon needs and cannot be keyed out cleanly, because the gloss and drop shadow blend into that background.

Palette sampled from your art: body #E8EEF2, edge #A6B4C0, visor #131A22, eyes #6FEFEF, gauge #4FD06A / #E9E24F / #F02F30.

To draw the logo exactly

Best: the vector source — SVG, PDF, AI or a Figma link. Then every size is exact, forever, and the print and favicon cases come free.

Good enough: a PNG export at 512px or larger with a transparent background and no drop shadow.

Neither? I redraw it as flat vector from the screenshot. The geometry is simple and I have the palette, so it will be recognisably the same character — but a flat interpretation, not the glossy render. Worth deciding deliberately: the gloss is what a vector logo cannot carry into a 16px tray or a one-colour print.
